newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia parliament to vote on cabinet Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia parliament to vote on cabinet Thursday.

text.p: The Slovenian parliament will vote on prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek's new cabinet on February 6, three months after inconclusive general elections, the general secretary's office said on Monday.
The vote, which may be preceded by a debate, will start at 10 a.m. (0900 GMT).
Parliamentary questioning of ministerial candidates, which began on January 28, will end later on Monday with the hearing of agriculture minister nominee Joze Protner.
So far 11 ministerial hopefuls have gained committee approval and six have failed.

Among key posts, finance minister nominee Mitja Gaspari and interior minister candidate Polonca Dobrajc failed to gain support, while foreign minister candidate Zoran Thaler and economic affairs nominee Metod Dragonja gained approval.
Nevertheless, sources close to Drnovsek said the Liberal Democrat leader was confident of winning Thursday's parliamentary vote without making any changes to his proposed ministerial team.
Drnovsek, prime minister since April 1992, succeeded in forming a broad coalition with a one-vote majority 10 days ago.
His government comprises the centre-left Liberal Democrats, former communists the United List of Social Democrats, the Desus party representing pensioners and the Nationalist Party.
The so-called Spring alliance of three rightist parties, which holds 44 of the 90 parliamentay seats, has said it will oppose Drnovsek's proposed line-up.
If the alliance succeeds in voting down Drnovsek, the prime minister must present a changed government list within 10 days.
The new government will be Slovenia's third since independence from the former Yugoslavia in 1991.
